review_scope: Publisher-side evidence review of the token-usage-meter guide. All 36 inventory blocks were re-checked against the primary sources listed below and eight content corrections were applied before this receipt was signed: (1) the OpenAI cache field path was fixed from prompt_tokens_details.* to the documented input_tokens_details.cached_tokens / cache_write_tokens; (2) the unsupported '9x on cache-hit rate alone' and 'nine times more' comparisons were replaced with the bounded ~10x multiplier effect; (3) the worked example was recomputed from published Sonnet 5 rates ($2.32, against ~$5.20 for the same tokens charged fresh) and the arithmetic is now shown; (4) the 'roughly 10%' cache-read statement now notes the per-model exceptions (0.025x Fable 5.1/Mythos 5.1, 0.05x Opus 5.5/Sonnet 5.5); (5) the cache-write row now states the real 1.25x/2x premiums instead of an unspecified 'write premium'; (6) the p95 trap was reworded to match the spec, which forbids the modality breakdown rather than merely warning about it; (7) all eight GitHub star counts and licences were replaced with GitHub API values read on 2026-10-07, and the table now carries that snapshot date; (8) a Sources section with the primary links was added, because the article previously carried no outbound citations. Schema partial, front matter and cover were checked against the article and are unchanged apart from this text. No first-party benchmark or test is claimed anywhere in the article.

claims.note: Title and meta description only; '2026' is the publication year, not a claimed data vintage, and the description restates the article's own definition.

Token field names and write premiums re-read from both provider docs: Anthropic lists cache_read_input_tokens / cache_creation_input_tokens with 1.25x (5m) and 2x (1h) write multipliers, OpenAI lists input_tokens_details.cached_tokens / cache_write_tokens.

The 10% cache-read rate and the resulting ~10x overstatement were checked against Anthropic's 0.1x cache-read multiplier; an earlier 9x figure was corrected because it understated the multiplier's effect.
Illustrative order of magnitude for calls in one task ('a single task can issue 30 model calls'), stated as an example rather than a measured count.
The claim that Anthropic and OpenAI responses carry token counts was verified against the response usage examples in both prompt-caching documents.

Every field named here (result.context_wrapper.usage, requests, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, request_usage_entries, cached_tokens, cache_write_tokens, reasoning_tokens) plus ModelSettings(include_usage=True), RunResult.to_state() and the nested Agent.as_tool() roll-up exception were read from the OpenAI Agents SDK usage page.

Anthropic admin API details re-read: bucket_width 1d/1h/1m with default limits 7/24/60 and maximums 31/168/1,440, grouping by model, workspace_id, api_key_id, inference_geo and speed (fast-mode beta header), /v1/organizations/cost_report in USD cents with daily granularity only, and data typically within 5 minutes.

Checked against the semantic-conventions CHANGELOG v1.42.0 entry (GenAI conventions moved to open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai, released 2026-06-12) and the GenAI repo's Development status banners; all gen_ai.* definitions remain Development while error.type, server.address and server.port are Stable.
Section heading only; no factual assertion.

The 200-vs-300 p95 example and the rule that per-operation histograms are deliberately not broken down by modality were taken from the token-metrics spec note; an earlier draft implied the modality dimension IS added, which the spec forbids, and the wording was corrected.

Boundary arrays compared entry by entry with the spec: per-operation token histograms use powers of four up to 67,108,864, gen_ai.invoke_agent.duration is 0.1 to 409.6s, and gen_ai.client.operation.duration is 0.01 to 81.92s.

Formula structure is arithmetic, not a sourced claim; the 0.10 cache-read multiplier inside it is Anthropic's published rate and the write multiplier is left as a named variable because it is 1.25x or 2x depending on TTL. Re-hashed after labeling the fenced formula block as text so the CI Hugo renderer (0.146.0) emits <pre><code> rather than a GoAT diagram; arithmetic unchanged.

Recomputed from Anthropic's published Sonnet 5 rates ($2/MTok input, $0.20/MTok cache read, $10/MTok output): 0.8M x 2 + 1.6M x 0.2 + 0.04M x 10 = $2.32. The earlier 'nine times more at full input rate' comparison was corrected to the honest contrast of roughly $5.20 for the same session, since only the 1.6M cached tokens change price.

Langfuse's infer-then-ingest behaviour, the o1 reasoning-model limitation, the requirement that usage keys match the model definition's keys, and generation/embedding-only cost were re-read from the token-and-cost-tracking page.
Illustrative size for an unfiltered tool dump ('100K tokens'); framed as an example of the failure pattern, not a measured result.
Illustrative ratio split ('40% of spend is transcript replay, 25% is one unfiltered log dump') presented as what category tagging reveals, not a measured breakdown.

LiteLLM enforcement details verified: max_budget and budget_duration per key/user/team, budget_reset_at in the key schema, automatic provider-tier pricing (Vertex PayGo/priority, Bedrock service tiers, Azure base-model mapping) when the response carries tier metadata, and the documented requirement to sync model pricing from the upstream repository.

OpenMeter's CloudEvents usage-event ingestion, SUM aggregation with groupBy, Apache-2.0 licence and the four-component self-host (API + workers with Kafka, ClickHouse and PostgreSQL) were confirmed in the docs and repository README; Trigger.dev and Requestly appear as named production customers on OpenMeter's own site.

All eight GitHub star counts and licences re-read from the GitHub API on 2026-10-07: LiteLLM 60,295 (custom licence), Langfuse 35,489 (custom), MLflow 28,306 (Apache-2.0), OpenLLMetry 7,474 (Apache-2.0), Helicone 6,206 (Apache-2.0), OpenLIT 2,829 (Apache-2.0), OpenMeter 2,371 (Apache-2.0), GenAI semconv 414 (Apache-2.0). Each figure was corrected to the API value, and the table now carries a 2026-10-07 snapshot date because star counts change daily.
Editorial interpretation of the table's asymmetry; no independent measurement is asserted.
Operational instruction for logging the raw usage payload; no first-party result is claimed.
Operational instruction for attaching business metadata at write time.
Operational instruction to compute and store cost at log time with a versioned price table.
Operational instruction to store atomic request records and aggregate on read.
Operational instruction to reconcile monthly; the four named discrepancy sources are stated as the common causes, not as a measured distribution.
Illustrative contrast ('document summarization' costing 12x 'chat') used to explain why per-feature cost matters, not a measured ratio.
The ~10% cache-read rate and the point that a cache-hit-rate gain beats most prompt-engineering work follow from Anthropic's published 0.1x multiplier.
Cache-read pricing compared with the full input rate; the 'up to 10x' bound now matches Anthropic's 0.1x multiplier after the earlier 9x figure was corrected.
Illustrative call count for a single run ('the 34-call run around it'); used to make the run-versus-call point, not reported as a measurement.
Histogram mis-summing behaviour and the 200-instead-of-300 figure are the spec's own worked example of why modality must not dimension a per-operation histogram.

Renaming risk verified: the move to the dedicated repository is the v1.42.0 breaking-change entry, and every gen_ai.* definition still carries Development status, so no deprecation window is guaranteed.
Closing editorial judgement about practice; no factual or performance claim.
FAQ answer re-checked against the admin API page: daily aggregate dashboards, no per-agent attribution, default 7 daily buckets, daily-only cost report granularity.
FAQ cache-savings answer restated from Anthropic's rates with the worked example recomputed at Sonnet 5's published prices and the same corrected ~$5.20 fresh-price comparison.

FAQ answer on gen_ai.* versus raw provider fields: dashboard-schema advice, the Development status of every gen_ai.* attribute as of October 2026, the absence of a deprecation window, and the spec's deliberate decision not to define dollar cost.
Bibliography block only; each listed document is the primary evidence for the claims above and the list itself asserts no independent fact beyond the citation.

pricing.note: Anthropic rates and multipliers taken from the published prompt-caching pricing table, OpenAI's cached-input discount from its prompt-caching guide; the article deliberately leaves the cache-write multiplier as a variable because it is 1.25x for a 5-minute write or 2x for 1 hour.
